headline: TransDigm beats ($12.44 vs $12.21) and guides 2027; Sea and On beat on sales but slide premarket; Rocket Lab's record quarter meets a wider loss; CoreWeave tonight
top_call: TransDigm, the airplane-parts toll booth, earned $12.44 a share vs $12.21 expected on sales up 23% and put out its first fiscal 2027 guide. Sea beat on revenue ($8.58B vs $8.05B) but missed on EPS, On's beat leaned on a tariff refund, and last night Rocket Lab posted record sales with a wider loss while AST SpaceMobile missed on both lines. Plain-English explainers below, plus CoreWeave tonight.
subject: The Daily Five — Tue Nov 10: TransDigm beats ($12.44 vs $12.21) and guides 2027
backdrop: Monday's rebound: the S&P 500 had its best day since April as dip-buyers returned to AI and chip stocks (AMD +13%, the chip index's biggest gain since July), even as Nvidia fell more than 4% on news of an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. Futures are mixed ahead of this morning's October CPI, per Investing.com.
on_deck_sub: Still to report today, Nov 10 (D-Wave's results weren't out at 7 AM ET), with Wall Street's EPS estimates per Yahoo Finance

ai.headline: Nvidia fell more than 4% Monday after announcing an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, who told staff he had a relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a spy for China; shares ticked higher after hours
ai.why: The AI trade's bellwether now has a headline risk that has nothing to do with chips. Trump said he believes Huang 'will be in good shape.'

ai.headline: Anthropic circulated IPO terms of about 867 million shares at $70-80 (up to $69.3 billion), then retracted the pricing as inaccurate, Reuters reported; formal marketing could start Tuesday
ai.why: The biggest AI IPO on the calendar just had a typo worth billions. CoreWeave reports tonight into the same mood.

ai.headline: Chip stocks ripped Monday: AMD +13.3%, Monolithic Power +16.6%, Astera Labs +13.7%, Applied Materials +11.4%, as the S&P 500 posted its best day since April
ai.why: Deutsche Bank says tech positioning had fallen below its post-Liberation Day lows. When everyone is already out, the only trade left is back in.
